question_text:
A particle is moving in a straight line with velocity given by $v(t) = t^3 - 3t^2 \text{e}^{0.05t}$, where $t \geqslant 0$ is in seconds, and distance units are in metres.

Use technology to find:

subparts.stem: the greatest speed reached by the particle in the first 4 seconds of motion

mark_breakdown.desc: Using technology to find the maximum value of $|v(t)|$ on $0 \le t \le 4$, giving $\approx 5.66\text{ ms}^{-1}$ at $t \approx 2.39$

subparts.solution:
$$\text{speed} = |v(t)|$$
Using technology, the maximum of $|v(t)|$ over $0 \le t \le 4$ is $\approx 5.66\text{ ms}^{-1}$ when $t \approx 2.39$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Speed is the absolute value of velocity: $\text{speed} = |v(t)|$. To find the maximum speed, locate the absolute maximum of $|v(t)|$ on the given interval.
step_by_step: Plot $y = |x^3 - 3x^2 e^{0.05x}|$ on a graphing calculator for $0 \le x \le 4$.
Find the local maximum / peak of the absolute value curve.
Identify the maximum speed value and the corresponding time.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Looking for the maximum of $v(t)$ instead of $|v(t)|$, which would ignore negative velocity with large magnitude.

subparts.stem: the total distance travelled by the particle in the first 4 seconds of motion.

mark_breakdown.desc: Evaluating the integral numerically using technology to get $\approx 12.5\text{ m}$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Total distance traveled is the integral of speed over time: $\int_{t_1}^{t_2} |v(t)|\,dt$.
step_by_step: State the integral for total distance: $\int_0^4 |v(t)|\,dt$.
Use the numerical integration feature on the GDC for $\int_0^4 |x^3 - 3x^2 e^{0.05x}|\,dx$.
Round to three significant figures: $12.5\text{ m}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Integrating $v(t)$ without the absolute value, which calculates displacement instead of total distance.
